query: I am staffing Kilnwick for the first time. Who is it intended to help, who makes the firing decisions, and what can I actually accept from a visitor?
Why does Kilnwick need the clay product rather than the maker's assurance that a piece will be fine, and which work can go into the pilot?
At Kilnwick, what information must go on the incoming tray card, who can accept it into a load, and when may the maker collect it?
Has the new Kilnwick key-holder rota changed who may run an evening firing, or is the current pilot still in force?
Before the witness load, what did Kilnwick hope to offer in the evening and when did it hope to open?
Explain Pedalbrook to a new depot volunteer: whom does borrowing serve, who coordinates it, and what must be true before a cycle leaves?
Why can a Pedalbrook volunteer not treat the padded front box as enough to permit a child passenger, and what use did the committee actually approve?
For Pedalbrook, tell the return volunteer why a closed borrowing entry may still leave the cycle unavailable and what the borrower should have completed before its outgoing handover.
Who signed off the Pedalbrook child-passenger exception after the shop sent its kit picture?
For Kilnwick and Pedalbrook respectively, whom should a new volunteer contact, and does signing up at their shared fair authorize either kiln operation or passenger carriage?
